claims.statement: Dynamic headspace of white hyacinths identified benzyl acetate and alpha-farnesene as major constituents, with additional odor-relevant minor compounds and trace pyrazines detected by sniffing.
claims.scope_limit: Publisher abstract only. Exact cultivar and botanical authentication were not established from the accessible record. Sampling artefacts and adsorbent discrimination matter; no extract identity or perfume ratio is established.

claims.statement: The corrected Tilia study reports species- and stage-dependent volatile profiles for T. cordata, T. tomentosa and T. miqueliana, retaining unidentified peaks.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed corrected abstract, selected results and 45 C enclosed-vial HS-SPME method reviewed. Chromatographic areas are not odor contributions. Descriptor lookup is not a primary sensory panel. Must be read with the 2023 correction.

claims.statement: The correction identifies incomplete original Table 2 data and updates the abstract, dependent results, tables, figures and parts of the discussion and methods.
claims.scope_limit: Publisher-indexed correction reviewed; direct retrieval was rate-limited. This is a companion correction, not another independent study. Uncorrected counts must not be reused.

claims.statement: The manufacturer describes Boronia megastigma absolute through green cassis, hay, fruit-floral and woody facets; its extraction uses open flowers and fine leaves.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed manufacturer page reviewed after direct timeouts. Absolute, Heart Absolute and Leaf Absolute are listed separately, without comparative grade data. Extraction solvent does not prove supplied carrier or concentration.

claims.statement: IFF identifies this Spartium junceum flower absolute with honeyed, dried-fruit, hay and malt facets.
claims.scope_limit: Solvent extraction followed by ethyl-alcohol purification describes the process, not final stock strength. No equivalent Cytisus identity, performance protocol, lot composition or dose is supplied.

claims.statement: Six Nelumbo nucifera accessions showed organ-dependent profiles: petals differed from stamens and receptacles, with 1,4-dimethoxybenzene prominent in the latter organs.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed methods and conclusion reviewed, including excised first-day tissues and sealed-vial HS-SPME at 37 C. No human odor contribution, perfume dose or intact ambient emission calibration is admitted.

claims.statement: The studied Nymphaea prolifera flower emissions were rich in anisole, guaiacol, veratrole and methoxyanisole, with organ and temporal differences.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed abstract and selected emission results reviewed. Mother, daughter and granddaughter flowers remain distinct. Ecology and chemical abundance do not establish human liking or a universal water-lily accord.

claims.statement: The study examines Nymphaea 'Paul Stetson' stamens across three developmental stages and reports changing volatile patterns.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed abstract, sampling and 60 C HS-SPME sections reviewed. This is laboratory-prepared stamen headspace, not an intact flower at ambient conditions. No species assignment beyond the named cultivar, GC-O claim or human intensity calibration is admitted.

claims.statement: Attached Phalaenopsis flowers showed light- and time-dependent monoterpene emissions; P. violacea and named hybrids did not respond identically.
claims.scope_limit: Abstract, plant material, collection methods and selected results reviewed. The paper alternates KHM221 and KHM2212 and contains differing photoperiod descriptions; preserve unresolved details, not a universal orchid profile. No perfumery calibration.

claims.statement: The named Cymbidium hybrid showed different organ profiles, with linalool prominent in petals and sepals.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed abstract, organ results and sliced-flower preparation reviewed. Chromatographic area percentages are not perfume ratios or perceived odor fractions. Some counts differ between prose and tables; no numeric transcription or whole-orchid generalization is admitted.

claims.statement: Sweetheart lychee was studied using SAFE, GC-O/MS and AEDA; floral and fruity sensory attributes coexisted with odor-active sulfur and green-associated compounds.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed abstract reviewed; full extraction details and tables not reviewed. Dilution factors are not recipe ratios. The reported food attributes cannot establish perfume fidelity or liking; metadata and original summaries only.

claims.statement: GC-O and sulfur-selective analysis of Mauritius, Brewster and Hak Ip found cultivar-dependent sulfur profiles associated with different cabbage and garlic ratings.
claims.scope_limit: Primary abstract reviewed only. Association does not show that sulfur addition improves perfume. These cultivars are not Sweetheart; no concentration or preference claim transfers to ethanol.

claims.statement: HS-SPME/GC-IT-MS of five Portuguese Ficus carica varieties distinguished pulp and peel from leaves in semiquantitative volatile profiles.
claims.scope_limit: Publisher abstract and introductory scope reviewed. This is not GC-O; leaves, pulp and peel cannot be merged. Latex was not the measured matrix. No whole-perfume sensory equivalence or mass-fraction conversion.

claims.statement: GC-MS-O and AEDA in Sarilop and Bursa Siyahi found cultivar- and tissue-dependent aroma-active profiles in fresh pulp and peel.
claims.scope_limit: Publisher abstract reviewed; subscription methods not reviewed. AEDA rank is not ingredient dose. Leaves, latex, dried fig and perfume release are outside this evidence.

claims.statement: Cydonia oblonga Round and Oblong cultivars differed in free and bound volatiles; the authors associate a tobacco off-flavor after processing with megastigmatrienone-II.
claims.scope_limit: Indexed abstract and highlights only. Hydrolysis and full methods are not reviewed. Bound precursors are not fresh-fruit emissions; food OAVs do not transfer to perfume. Pseudocydonia sinensis is a different target.

claims.statement: Biolandes identifies F0420 as Evernia prunastri absolute with woody warmth and a powdery facet in chypre contexts.
claims.scope_limit: Product identity and odor paragraph reviewed. Solvent, carrier and lot composition are not given. Broad persistence wording is not admitted as a measurement or safety clearance.

claims.statement: Biolandes identifies F0080 as Pseudevernia furfuracea absolute and describes a drier, woodier and less powdery effect than its oakmoss extract.
claims.scope_limit: Exact manufacturer grade only. The comparator is not explicitly coded F0420 and no controlled sensory comparison is reported. IFRA wording is not independent clearance; no solvent or carrier is established.

claims.statement: IFF's Styrax benzoin gum-resin extract is described through balsamic vanilla, powdery cinnamic and cereal-associated facets.
claims.scope_limit: Ethyl alcohol is the extraction solvent, not established final stock carrier. Botanical product identity remains distinct from Siam despite a shared broad CAS. No universal strength or sweetness ranking.

claims.statement: IFF identifies a molecularly distilled Myroxylon balsamum var. pereirae product with powdery sweet balsamic, vanilla, cinnamon and amber facets.
claims.scope_limit: This exact oil grade is not crude balsam, a resinoid or natural Tolu. Qualitative component names are not a complete composition; no dose, skin performance or safety clearance.

claims.scope_limit: Identity evidence for the reported preparations only; no clinical, supplier-grade or safety transfer.

claims.scope_limit: Hexane concrete is not a living-flower headspace, monoi product or coconut accord.

claims.scope_limit: Species and sampled flowers do not establish a universal frangipani absolute or coconut profile.

claims.statement: Early and late experimental ylang distillation fractions differ in ester/alcohol and sesquiterpene composition.
claims.scope_limit: A deeper review of the existing ylang source, not an independent study; experimental fractions are not automatically retail Extra or III.

claims.statement: The peony study compares cultivar-dependent floral profiles using heated cut-petal sampling and water-based threshold references.
claims.scope_limit: A deeper review of the existing study, not new human gas-dose data; water thresholds cannot calibrate perfume headspace.

claims.statement: The Freesia study samples detached petals under heated conditions; cultivar profiles differ despite shared linalool.

claims.statement: The study reports species-dependent lilac-compound stereoisomer patterns, including Syringa vulgaris.
claims.scope_limit: Not a complete lilac formula; moth responses and chemical isomers do not establish human receptor equivalence.

claims.statement: Lonicera japonica emissions change with anthesis and time, with floral-terpenic and green components among the reported volatiles.

claims.statement: The sweet-pea study reports floral alcohols and terpenes, but its column comparisons also differ in elapsed sampling time.

claims.statement: Fresh and dried Magnolia alba preparations were examined under distinct sampling and heating conditions.

claims.statement: Selected entries distinguish fruity, green, nutty and stone-fruit functions and explicitly supplied solutions.

profiles.label: Rooty / mineral iris
profiles.clue: Keep iris primary; compare a root-texture addition against the unmodified control, not an automatic vetiver replacement.

profiles.label: Buttery / waxy orris
profiles.clue: An irone assay, natural orris butter and a prepared dilution are not the same material.

profiles.label: Lipstick / cosmetic iris
profiles.clue: Compare cosmetic texture without automatically adding vanilla or extra sweetness.

profiles.label: Transparent / luminous iris
profiles.clue: Airy support must preserve the iris recognizer; clarity is a smelling hypothesis, not a diffusion score.

profiles.label: Woody / tobacco / suede iris
profiles.clue: Woody iris grades may connect to suede or tobacco, but those accents must not replace iris.

profiles.label: Violet petals
profiles.clue: Violet petals and violet leaf are different targets; individual ionone sensitivity can change their perception.

profiles.label: Powdery / candied violet
profiles.clue: Test powder and sweetness separately rather than assuming every violet request should be candied.

profiles.label: Green violet leaf
profiles.clue: Green violet leaf is not a substitute for violet petals or an automatic iris-powder requirement.

profiles.label: Dimensional pear / apple fruit
profiles.clue: Make the fruit itself more dimensional; test peel, flesh and continuity without adding an unrelated bouquet.

profiles.label: Fruit-to-musk continuation
profiles.clue: A pear-related musk facet is a continuity hypothesis, not proof that the fruit lasts on skin.

profiles.label: Projection / temporal performance
profiles.clue: Match the application first; source dose, delivered concentration and perceived projection are different.

profiles.label: Lavender product and facet identity
profiles.clue: Choose the intended lavender register and role before choosing its base; lavender is not synonymous with fougere or Ambrox.

profiles.label: Citrus / herbal lavender
profiles.clue: Keep citrus, the aromatic recognizer and its heart bridge separate; a fresh goal does not mandate amberwoods.

profiles.label: Classical coumarin / moss lavender
profiles.clue: The lavender-coumarin-moss relationship is a classical construction, not the compulsory recipe for all lavender.

profiles.label: Green barbershop lavender
profiles.clue: Compare a green geranium/herb bridge against sweetness; do not turn a dry barbershop target into gourmand lavender.

profiles.label: Lavender / vanilla / resin contrast
profiles.clue: Resinous vanilla warmth is a different decision from mineral ambergris support; keep the lavender contrast legible.

profiles.label: Soft musky lavender
profiles.clue: Choose a supported musk texture, not a mandatory multi-musk stack or a large woody-amber fill.

profiles.label: Lavender / orange blossom
profiles.clue: Treat orange blossom and lavender as distinct recognizers; do not replace that relationship with a generic white-floral bouquet.

profiles.label: Lavender / jasmine / sandalwood
profiles.clue: Test the floral bridge and creamy wood return separately from extra sweetness or stronger lavender.

profiles.label: Vanilla-led gourmand lavender
profiles.clue: A vanilla-led lavender is an explicit gourmand branch, not the default explanation of richness.

profiles.label: Apple / aromatic lavender
profiles.clue: Protect apple and lavender from generic tropical drift; the current Layton record is a reference, not a formula.

profiles.label: Pineapple / patchouli lavender
profiles.clue: Test the fruit-aromatic contrast separately from sugar and patchouli loading.

profiles.label: Lavender / iris / violet
profiles.clue: Separate iris root, violet leaf/petals and lavender roles; an iris note does not require held Orris Liquid.

profiles.label: Lavender / dry incense
profiles.clue: Separate resin incense from phenolic smoke, leather and Ambrox; compare the dry bridge against the control.

profiles.label: Lavender / dark wood or oud
profiles.clue: A darker wood branch must preserve lavender rather than become an oud perfume with a brief aromatic opening.

profiles.label: Lavender / coffee / milk
profiles.clue: Keep roast, milk texture and sweetness independently adjustable; no ingredient is mandated by the word gourmand.

profiles.label: Lavender / licorice
profiles.clue: A licorice effect is not proof of a particular anise material or sweetener.

profiles.label: Spiced lavender / wood
profiles.clue: Keep the spice recognizer and wood return separate; Elixir's description is not evidence of an Ambrox-free formula.

profiles.label: Lavender / mineral ambergris
profiles.clue: An Ambrox-associated lavender needs its own herb/floral bridge; a no-Ambrox brief takes precedence over this optional support clue.

profiles.label: Ginger / citrus / lavandin
profiles.clue: Use ginger as a specific spicy-citrus contrast rather than adding several unrelated spices.

profiles.label: Fruity / ambrette versus warm woody musk support
profiles.clue: Test the fruity bridge and warm musk role separately; two musk names do not prove two useful functions, greater richness or longer wear.

profiles.label: Ambergris / resinous amber / woody-amber distinction
profiles.clue: First decide which amber character the brief actually asks for; do not substitute high-impact amberwood for ambergris or resinous warmth merely to chase performance.

profiles.label: Citrus recognizer with exact process / grade
profiles.clue: Keep species and expressed/distilled/FCF/terpeneless grade explicit. A citrus role can be explored without inventing lot composition or treating every grade as equivalent.

profiles.label: Resinous amber, not mineral ambergris
profiles.clue: Keep vanillic balsam and resin/leather warmth independently adjustable; do not solve every amber brief with an amberwood.

profiles.label: Named musk-register comparison
profiles.clue: Compare the named musk roles using omission, not an ingredient-count or synergy score.

profiles.label: Exact processed bergamot grade
profiles.clue: Review the actual grade before borrowing process claims. This card grants no safety clearance.

profiles.label: Transparent floral support versus recognizer
profiles.clue: Keep the requested flower primary. Transparent support is a challenger, not a mandatory generic bouquet.

profiles.label: Warm sandalwood register
profiles.clue: Keep creamy/warm wood distinct from dry cedar or sharp amberwood; preserve the target's primary identity.

profiles.label: Leaf/stem modifier boundary
profiles.clue: Specify leaf, stem or fruit before adding a green modifier; no automatic leafy dose for a green adjective.

profiles.label: Explicit chypre chassis and branch
profiles.clue: Preserve the explicit chypre branch; modern alternatives need their own omission/contrast evidence.

profiles.label: Leather register without automatic smoke
profiles.clue: Do not substitute smoky tar for soft suede, or make iris-leather cease to be iris-led.

profiles.label: Vanilla/tonka versus roast and milk
profiles.clue: Choose the food register; keep roast, dairy texture and sweetness separate. Do not add sweetness just because the brief says rich.

profiles.label: Pear-first architecture reference axes
profiles.clue: Use pear/citrus/osmanthus and pear/freesia as different clues. Keep apple and lychee subordinate to the locked target; prevent rose, apricot or shampoo drift.
